lines.trans: Daydreaming right in the middle of rehearsal—wait, why is she not stepping out of the way!
Why is Cindy in this bed? Then where is Senior Ye-jin?
Why did she have to tumble down into that opening—she scared the life out of me!
I thought you were the one badly hurt, senior—anyway, what a relief!
Hey, I got hurt too!
Only because Cindy got hurt way worse do I look fine—I am plenty injured too, I am a patient!
Wait—why are you dripping with so much sweat, Joon-mo?
Oh, it is nothing.
Cindy and I arrived at the exact same time, yet they rushed her in for every test first.
Look at me still sitting here—is this not celebrity preferential treatment?

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'rehearsal', commonly used in broadcasting and performing arts.

examples.trans: There is a rehearsal before the performance.
The rehearsal starts at 2 p.m.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 걔는 어떻게 된 게 중간이 없어, 극단적인 애교!
examples.trans: Somehow she has no middle ground whatsoever—just extreme cuteness!
Here the word for 'middle ground' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.trans: She is so two-faced like that!
Here the word for 'like that, so' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 리허설 중간에도 저렇게 딴생각을 하고 있으시구나, 쟤 왜 안 비켜!
examples.trans: Daydreaming right in the middle of rehearsal—wait, why is she not stepping out of the way!
Here the word for 'daydreaming, other thoughts' is key.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.text: 그냥 내버려 둬, 쟤 완전 취했어.
examples.trans: Just leave him alone, he is completely wasted.
The topic of that guy/girl came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 리허설 중간에도 저렇게 딴생각을 하고 있으시구나, 쟤 왜 안 비켜!
examples.trans: Daydreaming right in the middle of rehearsal—wait, why is she not stepping out of the way!
This expression comes from 'does she not move aside!'.
Did you hear about this Ms.?
I was busy today because of Ms..

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그러면.

examples.trans: Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for location.

examples.trans: Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그 아이 ('that child/kid'); used only for younger people or close peers.

examples.trans: Are you close with her?
He is late every day.

related.gloss: this kid / he or she (near speaker)
that kid / he or she (over there)

meanings.note: Points to a place near the listener, and in casual or brisk speech is used to call out to someone whose name you do not know. RR: geogi.

examples.trans: Hey, you there, just a moment!
How is the atmosphere there?
I want to fall off, you know right now.
How about trying to fall off, you know together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 걔는 왜 거기로 떨어지냐고, 나 진짜 깜놀했잖아!
examples.trans: Why did she have to tumble down into that opening—she scared the life out of me!
This expression comes from 'got totally startled!'.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

다치다.gloss: to get hurt, to be injured

meanings.note: Used for physical injuries

examples.trans: I fell and hurt my knee.
Be careful not to get hurt.

meanings.note: When used with 알다/모르다, it means knowing or not knowing a fact or how to do something.

examples.trans: I knew it would rain.
Do you know how to swim?

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

examples.text: 아무튼 걱정하지 마십시오. 주소 공유 관계는 발설하지 않겠습니다.
examples.trans: Anyway, please do not worry. I will not breathe a word about the address-sharing arrangement.

examples.text: 아무튼 저 촬영장에서도 피디님만 보고 가요. 수고하세요.
examples.trans: Anyway, I am going to the set counting only on you. Keep up the good work.
Did you hear about this is fortunate?
I was busy today because of is fortunate.
This is my friend Minsu.
He/she did it all.

meanings.note: Contraction of 이 아이; used when introducing or referring to someone younger or close
Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 신디가 월등히 많이 다쳐서 그렇지 나도 충분히 다쳤거든, 나도 환자야!
examples.trans: Only because Cindy got hurt way worse do I look fine—I am plenty injured too, I am a patient!
Here the word for 'far more, by far' is key.

meanings.en: a lot, much, in large quantity
meanings.note: Adverbial form of 많다 (to be many/much)

examples.trans: I did a lot of work today.
Please eat plenty and enjoy.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

examples.text: 오해할 수 있는 상황인 거 내가 충분히 알아.
examples.trans: I fully understand that this is a situation you could misunderstand.

examples.text: 충분히 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (fully, plenty), we will get good results.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 신디가 월등히 많이 다쳐서 그렇지 나도 충분히 다쳤거든, 나도 환자야!
examples.trans: Only because Cindy got hurt way worse do I look fine—I am plenty injured too, I am a patient!
Here the word for 'am a patient!' is key.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Adverbial form of 이렇다.
Used to emphasize degree.

examples.trans: You can do it like this.
Why is it so cold today?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 근데 그 찰떡이 여기서 땀과 눈물과 피와 수명을 쏟아야 만들어지는 거야.
examples.trans: Except that fine rice cake is only made by pouring your sweat, tears, blood, and lifespan into this room.
Here the word for 'sweat and' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 넌 근데 왜 이렇게 땀을 많이 흘리니?
examples.trans: Wait—why are you dripping with so much sweat, Joon-mo?
This expression comes from 'are you sweating?'.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.
Did you hear about this at the same time?
I was busy today because of at the same time.

examples.text: 조금만 더 가면 금방 도착할 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: If we go just a little farther, we should arrive soon.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 도착하다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (will arrive).

meanings.note: superlative adverb placed before an adjective or adverb

examples.text: 한국 음식 중에서 비빔밥을 제일 좋아해요.
examples.trans: Among Korean foods, I like bibimbap the most.
Today is the coldest day of this week.

meanings.en: first, before others, ahead of time
meanings.note: Indicates priority in order or time.

examples.trans: It's late, so I'll head in first.
Who arrived first?

examples.text: 선? 검사? 설마 검사가 예쁘기까지 하겠어?
examples.trans: A blind date? A prosecutor? Could a prosecutor really be pretty too?
The topic of prosecutor came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: Compound of 하다 (to do) and 주다 (to give).

examples.trans: Please help me (do helping for me).
Please do this for me.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?
Did you hear about this celebrity?
I was busy today because of celebrity.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 나 봐라, 이거 연예인 특혜 아니니?
examples.trans: Look at me still sitting here—is this not celebrity preferential treatment?
Here the word for 'special treatment' is key.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)
